summary: Paris is the capital of France [[web_d78712e345451b942555c838]] [[web_3954c8c48a7f18bf3990ce86]], and its population depends on which geographic definition is used: the city proper (commune) had 2,103,778 inhabitants in 2023 [[web_7a785252b8bcd3717872395e]], while the wider urban area holds roughly 11 million and the functional metropolitan area about 13.3 million [[web_b027a303cc0a26f62f829581]].

sections.title: The capital
sections.markdown: Paris is the capital of France and the seat of its national government. The President resides at the Élysée Palace, the Prime Minister at the Hôtel Matignon, and both houses of Parliament — the Senate in the Palais du Luxembourg and the National Assembly in the Palais Bourbon — sit in the city, along with France's highest courts [[web_d78712e345451b942555c838]]. Independent references concur: Wikipedia's Paris article describes Paris as the "Capital city in Île-de-France, France" [[web_d78712e345451b942555c838]], and WorldStats confirms in its FAQ that Paris is the capital of France [[web_3954c8c48a7f18bf3990ce86]].

sections.title: Population of the city proper
sections.markdown:
The authoritative figure comes from INSEE, France's national statistics institute. The 2023 census (RP2023) puts the Paris commune (INSEE code 75056) at 2,103,778 inhabitants, with a density of about 19,960 per km² [[web_7a785252b8bcd3717872395e]]. This figure is legally authenticated: the populations de référence 2023, in force from 1 January 2026 under décret n° 2025-1362, give the same 2,103,778 as the population municipale (plus 15,634 counted separately, for a total of 2,119,412) [[web_942c04b6ae83e6189f32b13d]] [[web_82c5e112d85d843f9fb914ab]]. A secondary source, WorldStats, estimates roughly 2.14 million as of 2026 and ranks Paris first in France [[web_3954c8c48a7f18bf3990ce86]] — consistent in magnitude with the INSEE figure, though the trend is downward: INSEE records an average annual decline of −0.6% between 2017 and 2023, driven by net out-migration (−1.2%/yr) partly offset by natural increase (+0.5%/yr) [[web_7a785252b8bcd3717872395e]].

The city's population has fluctuated over decades: 2,590,771 in 1968, a low of 2,125,246 in 1999, a rebound to 2,240,621 in 2012, then decline to 2,103,778 in 2023 [[web_942c04b6ae83e6189f32b13d]] [[web_b88b792206e59adc55fa8067]]. Wikipedia's Paris article gives slightly different recent figures (2,102,650 in January 2023, and 2,047,602 as of January 2026) [[web_d78712e345451b942555c838]] [[web_4862d14b8b81bb24a2a67b97]]; these minor discrepancies reflect different census vintages and estimation methods, but all sources agree the city proper holds roughly 2.0–2.1 million people.

sections.title: Wider geographies: which "Paris" population?
sections.markdown:
Any population figure must state its definition, because INSEE uses distinct statistical geographies [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]:

| Geography | Population (2023) | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| City proper (commune) | 2,103,778 | [[web_7a785252b8bcd3717872395e]] |
| Urban unit (unité urbaine) | 11,013,774 | [[web_b027a303cc0a26f62f829581]] |
| Île-de-France region | 12,463,067 | [[web_b027a303cc0a26f62f829581]] |
| Functional area (aire d'attraction) | 13,320,752 | [[web_b027a303cc0a26f62f829581]] |

These INSEE figures are corroborated exactly by Wikipedia's Demographics of Paris article [[web_4862d14b8b81bb24a2a67b97]]. A broader Wikipedia figure of 15,064,617 for the "Paris metropolitan area" reflects a wider statistical definition than the INSEE aire d'attraction and is a definitional difference, not a data conflict [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]]. Demographia's INSEE-derived series (10.46 million for the urbanized area in 2010) is consistent in scale with the urban unit figures, differing only in vintage [[web_9e44f470d29f84ea8938a23f]].

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.markdown: The capital of France is Paris, the seat of the national government and both houses of Parliament [[web_d78712e345451b942555c838]], a status also confirmed by WorldStats [[web_3954c8c48a7f18bf3990ce86]]. Its population is roughly 2.1 million within city limits (INSEE 2023: 2,103,778, legally in force since 1 January 2026) [[web_7a785252b8bcd3717872395e]] [[web_942c04b6ae83e6189f32b13d]], about 11 million in the continuous urban area, and about 13.3 million in the wider functional metropolitan area [[web_b027a303cc0a26f62f829581]]. The only material uncertainty is definitional — which "Paris" is meant — not factual: the commune, urban unit, and aire d'attraction are distinct INSEE statistical geographies [[web_a02c4c9a3a1d6ab86978fe0b]], and the underlying figures are consistent across INSEE primary sources [[web_7a785252b8bcd3717872395e]] [[web_b027a303cc0a26f62f829581]] and independent secondary references [[web_4862d14b8b81bb24a2a67b97]] [[web_3954c8c48a7f18bf3990ce86]].

claim.text: Paris is the capital of France, and its population depends on which geographic definition is used: the city proper (commune) had 2,103,778 inhabitants in 2023, while the wider urban area holds roughly 11 million and the functional metropolitan area about 13.3 million
Paris is the capital of France and the seat of its national government

The President resides at the Élysée Palace, the Prime Minister at the Hôtel Matignon, and both houses of Parliament — the Senate in the Palais du Luxembourg and the National Assembly in the Palais Bourbon — sit in the city, along with France's highest courts
Independent references concur: Wikipedia's Paris article describes Paris as the "Capital city in Île-de-France, France", and WorldStats confirms in its FAQ that Paris is the capital of France
The authoritative figure comes from INSEE, France's national statistics institute
The 2023 census (RP2023) puts the Paris commune (INSEE code 75056) at 2,103,778 inhabitants, with a density of about 19,960 per km²

This figure is legally authenticated: the populations de référence 2023, in force from 1 January 2026 under décret n° 2025-1362, give the same 2,103,778 as the population municipale (plus 15,634 counted separately, for a total of 2,119,412)

A secondary source, WorldStats, estimates roughly 2.14 million as of 2026 and ranks Paris first in France — consistent in magnitude with the INSEE figure, though the trend is downward: INSEE records an average annual decline of −0.6% between 2017 and 2023, driven by net out-migration (−1.2%/yr) partly offset by natural increase (+0.5%/yr)
The city's population has fluctuated over decades: 2,590,771 in 1968, a low of 2,125,246 in 1999, a rebound to 2,240,621 in 2012, then decline to 2,103,778 in 2023

Wikipedia's Paris article gives slightly different recent figures (2,102,650 in January 2023, and 2,047,602 as of January 2026); these minor discrepancies reflect different census vintages and estimation methods, but all sources agree the city proper holds roughly 2.0–2.1 million people
Any population figure must state its definition, because INSEE uses distinct statistical geographies
Geography: City proper (commune); Population (2023): 2,103,778; Source:
Geography: Urban unit (unité urbaine); Population (2023): 11,013,774; Source:
Geography: Île-de-France region; Population (2023): 12,463,067; Source:
Geography: Functional area (aire d'attraction); Population (2023): 13,320,752; Source:
These INSEE figures are corroborated exactly by Wikipedia's Demographics of Paris article

A broader Wikipedia figure of 15,064,617 for the "Paris metropolitan area" reflects a wider statistical definition than the INSEE aire d'attraction and is a definitional difference, not a data conflict
Demographia's INSEE-derived series (10.46 million for the urbanized area in 2010) is consistent in scale with the urban unit figures, differing only in vintage
The capital of France is Paris, the seat of the national government and both houses of Parliament, a status also confirmed by WorldStats

Its population is roughly 2.1 million within city limits (INSEE 2023: 2,103,778, legally in force since 1 January 2026), about 11 million in the continuous urban area, and about 13.3 million in the wider functional metropolitan area

The only material uncertainty is definitional — which "Paris" is meant — not factual: the commune, urban unit, and aire d'attraction are distinct INSEE statistical geographies, and the underlying figures are consistent across INSEE primary sources and independent secondary references
